transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, they say I’m here because of... the money. I used our savings on wood, lights, and all this display stuff. I just kept pushing the work, even after dark. I had to. I felt like if I stopped, the whole house—and the whole block, really—would lose its chance. But my family, they didn't see it that way.
Have you experienced periods like this before—times when you felt unusually energetic, spent money impulsively, or needed very little sleep—or is this the first time something like this has happened?

No, I... I don't think so. I mean, I've always liked to keep busy, but not like this. I've never gone and spent our savings like that before, or stayed up all night working on something. So, yeah, this is... this is the first time anything like this has happened. I just haven't ever felt this way before.
Have you ever had a period where you felt very sad, hopeless, or depressed that lasted for several days or longer?

No, I... I can't say that I have. I mean, everybody gets a little down sometimes, just with life, but not like what you're saying. I've never been stuck feeling sad or hopeless for days on end. I'm usually just a pretty steady guy. So, no, I haven't had anything like that.
How long has this period of high energy, working late into the night, and spending money been going on? Has it been days, weeks, or longer?

Well, I'd say it's been about three months now. Yeah, right around three months. It all started when the remodeling began and... well, everything in the house just got turned upside down. That's when I really got going with it.

During these three months, when you were working late into the night, did you actually need less sleep than usual—like feeling fine and rested after only 3 or 4 hours—or were you just too caught up in the work to go to bed, even though you might have felt tired?

I didn't need much sleep at all. I wasn't just staying up because I was busy—I honestly felt fine. Three or four hours, maybe, and I'd be up and ready to go again. I didn't feel tired the next day, either. I just felt like I had all the energy I needed to keep working.

During these three months when you were working on the house display, did you ever have any unusual beliefs or experiences—like feeling like you had special powers, or hearing or seeing things that others around you couldn't hear or see?

Well, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, if that's what you mean. But... I know people think I'm mixed up right now. I just know, I'm absolutely sure, that this neighborhood was picked for my last big civic art piece. That's what all the work on the house is for. 

And it's not just me making it up. Little things prove it to me every day. Like... the trucks slowing down when they drive past, or the neighbors always looking over the property line. They know it too. They know something big is happening here.

When you say the neighborhood was picked for your art piece and that the neighbors know something big is happening—if someone you trust told you they didn't see any evidence of that, would you be able to consider that maybe you might be wrong about it, or are you completely certain it's true no matter what anyone else says?

No, I wouldn't believe them. I know people think I'm mixed up right now, but I am completely certain. I'm absolutely sure this neighborhood was picked for my last big civic art piece. No matter what anyone says, I know it's true. The proof is right there—like I said, the trucks slowing down, the neighbors looking over the fence. They know it too, even if they won't admit it to you. I'm not wrong about this.

When you look back at things like the trucks slowing down or the neighbors looking over the fence, do you think there could be any other explanation for those things—like maybe the trucks just happen to slow down for traffic, or the neighbors are just curious about the remodeling—or do you think those things can only mean what you believe about the art piece?

There's no other explanation. I mean... I know people think I'm mixed up, but I'm sure this neighborhood was picked for my last big civic art piece. The trucks slowing down, the neighbors looking over... those little things prove they know it too. They aren't just curious. They know.

When these beliefs about the neighborhood being picked for your art piece started three months ago, did your mood feel elevated or unusually good at that same time, or did the beliefs come first and then your mood changed?

Well, the mood came first. Before I got so... charged up with all the remodeling plans, I wasn't seeing any special meaning in the trucks driving by or the neighbors looking over the fence. I just felt really good, really driven to start the work. Those signs, the proof that the neighborhood was chosen... that only started making sense to me after I was already deep into turning the house into my big civic project.
